text: 61 Danaë is a stony (S-type) asteroid located in the outer asteroid belt's background population, with a diameter of approximately 84 kilometers. It was discovered by French astronomer Hermann Goldschmidt on 9 September 1860 from his balcony in Paris, France. Goldschmidt was ill at the time and asked his colleague Robert Luther to name the asteroid, who named it after Danaë, the mother of Perseus in Greek mythology. Danaë holds the distinction of being the first asteroid to feature a diacritical character in its official name. The asteroid orbits the Sun with a period of 5.15 years and rotates once every 11.45 hours. A 1985 study of lightcurve data indicated that Danaë might have a moon; if it does, the main body would be an ellipsoid measuring 85 km × 80 km × 75 km (53 mi × 50 mi × 47 mi), and the moon would orbit 101 kilometers (63 mi) away, measuring 55 km × 30 km × 30 km (34 mi × 19 mi × 19 mi). Both the main body and the moon have a density of 1.1 g/cm³.
